content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a novel edge representation for oriented object detection and designs a regression loss, Edge Wasserstein distance loss, to alleviate the square-like problem. The representation and loss are general to rectangular, quadrilateral and polynomial regressions. The paper conducts experiments on the DOTA, HRSC2016, ICDAR2015 and MSRA-TD500 datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. It is the first time that edge representation is used for oriented object detection. The idea of modelling edges as different Gaussian Distributions is novel.
2. The edge representation and EWD loss are general in both oriented rectangular and polynomial regressions.

Weakness:
1. The paper is difficult to read. The symbols are confusing and inconsistent, for example, f_EWD in Eq. (14) is not explained and (\delta x, \delta y) in Eq. (14) is not in bold but the same symbol under Eq. (10) is in bold. Some subscripts are also missing, such as the subscript for c in Eq. (25). The authors should carefully check equations and mathematical descriptions in the paper.
2. The formats of citations are improper, which should be in brackets.
3. The paper only compares with peer methods which are based on RetinaNet and FCOS. There is no comparison with other SOTAs, such as two-stage methods, which cannot validate that the methods with EWD losses are better than others.
4. For objects with large aspect ratios in Table-2, EGWD and EDWD fail in some categories, for example, EDWD with RetinaNet and FCOS show lower performance than GWD and KLD. Besides, the average precision 5-AP is lower than that of KLD when the EWD losses are added to RetinaNet. Thus, it is hard to validate the effectiveness of the EWD losses on the targets with large aspect ratios.
5. In Section 3.2 and 3.3, the paper mentions that there will be more discussion for the variances of the width and height. However, I have not found the discussion on different choices of variances in the paper. The authors may miss this part.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper has poor readability in mathematical formulas and does not clarify some opinions clearly. Besides, the authors do not provide code. All make the paper not easy to reproduce.

The edge representation for oriented rectangles is novel but the Gaussian distribution assumption and Wasserstein distance loss have been used in recent work GWD.
content.summary_of_the_review: The motivation of the paper is clear and reasonable. However, the experiments are not completed and cannot well support the effectiveness of the EWD losses.

content.summary_of_the_paper: To alleviate the metric discontinuity and the square-like problem in regression loss for oriented object detection, this work proposes a novel oriented regression loss, termed as Wasserstein Distance (EWD) loss, which can be generalized to quadrilateral and polynomial regression scenarios. The experimental results are solid and look promising.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. The proposed Wasserstein Distance (EWD) loss succeeds in capturing the angular information and regressing the angle precisely. 
2. EWD is able to immune from both the angular periodicity and ambiguity of width and height, and handles the square-like problem in oriented object detection.
3. The edge representation can be general to rectangular, quadrilateral and polynomial regressions.
4. Authors theoretically develop the formulation of EWD loss on oriented bounding box occasions.

Weaknesses:

1. In the page 3, it shows that `the Gaussian representation degenerates for the squared OBoxs as the rotation of squares will not change their Gaussian representation’. As gaussian representation with rotational matrix is also defined by angles, please explain why it cannot be able to immune from the angular periodicity but the edge representation does?
2. Below the equation 3, \pi denotes the bipartite matching function. what is the form of cost function?
3. In term of edge representation, how to define the direction of edge?
4. In the equation of 5, please clarify the design choice of rotation matrix where S is represented by edge length.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality of the paper is good: it studies the fundamental task, oriented object detection in computer vision, and is supported by the theoretical foundations. However, there is still some ambiguity and the lack of details for reproducibility as mentioned in the weaknesses. Clarity needs to be improved.  Some sections are hard to follow due to not well-organized and formatted functions.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a new oriented box representation, a clockwise edge sequence, and a new oriented regression loss, Wasserstein Distance(EWD) loss, for the task of oriented object detection. Particularly, a 2-dimensional distribution is proposed to represent an oriented bounding box whose probability density function is only nonzero over the edges. In experiments, the proposed approach was evaluated on action detection benchmark datasets DOTA-1.0, HRSC2016, ICDAR2015, and MSRA-TD500.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength 

- presents a new oriented box representation and a new oriented regression loss for the task of oriented object detection

- benchmarks the performance of the proposed method on a set of datasets 

Weaknesses

- Novelty seems incremental. The edge Wasserstein distance loss seems like an extension of the Gaussian Wasserstein distance loss. But the formulation entails a set of approximations and simplifications. It is an unknown question how well the final formulation will fit to the original one. Also, it is not guaranteed that the decompositions will keep the constraints in an oriented box.

- Experiments seem lacking/unconvincing. From the figures and tables, it seems like the proposed approach only works for circular and near-square objects, but not for objects with large aspect ratios. More experiments (and analysis) need to be included to ablate and clarify on the drop of objects with large aspect ratios.

- Clarity needs to be improved. It seems like the paper was not well-organized and formatted, thus making some sections/parts hard to understand.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity needs to be improved. It seems like the paper was not well-organized and formatted, thus making some sections/parts hard to understand. 

Novelty seems incremental. The edge Wasserstein distance loss seems like an extension of the Gaussian Wasserstein distance loss. But the formulation entails a set of approximations and simplifications. It is an unknown question how well the final formulation will fit to the original one. Also, it is not guaranteed that the decompositions will keep the constraints in an oriented box.

Regarding reproducibility, the derivations are included but not the code. It might be better to release the code for good reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a new representation of an oriented box and a sensible formulation for solving the problem. But the novelty seems incremental, experiments seem lacking/unconvincing, and clarity needs to be improved.

content.title: Edge Wasserstein Distance Loss for Oriented Object Detection
content.TL;DR: This paper proposes a novel orinted object regression loss
content.abstract: Regression loss design is an essential topic for oriented object detection. Due to the periodicity of the angle and the ambiguity of width and height definition, traditional L1-distance losses and its variants have been suffered from the metric discontinuity and the square-like problem. As a solution, the distribution based methods show significant advantage by representing oriented boxes as distributions. Differing from exploited the Gaussian distribution to get analytical form of distance measure, we propose a novel oriented regression loss, Wasserstein Distance(EWD) loss, to alleviate the square-like problem.Specifically, for the oriented box representation,  we choose a specially-designed distribution whose probability density function is only nonzero over the edges. On this basis, we develop Wasserstein distance as the measure. Besides, based on the edge representation of oriented box, the EWD loss can be generalized to quadrilateral and polynomial regression scenery. Experiments on multiple popular datasets and different detectors show the effectiveness of the proposed method.
